<action type="say">
I’m not able to see your actual card or transactions from here, so I can’t file the dispute directly, but I can walk you through exactly what to do and what to say so your bank has what it needs.

Here’s how to handle a **duplicate Best Buy charge of $249.99 on Nov 2**:

1) Gather your evidence
- Screenshot or PDF of your card statement page showing:
  - Two separate Best Buy charges of **$249.99** on/around **Nov 2**.
- Any Best Buy receipt or order confirmation showing you were only charged once (if you have it).
- Note the **date**, **amount**, and **location/online** of the purchase.

2) File the dispute with your card issuer
Use whichever of these you can access fastest:

a) Online or mobile app  
- Go to your **credit card account**.  
- Find **“Transactions”** or **“Activity”**.  
- Tap the **Nov 2 Best Buy charge** (if both show, choose the one you believe is the duplicate; if unsure, you can mention that in your notes).  
- Look for **“Report a problem” / “Dispute this charge” / “Question this transaction.”**  
- When asked for the reason, choose:
  - **“Duplicate charge”** (or “I was charged twice for the same purchase”).  
- In the notes, you can write something close to this:
  > “I made a single purchase at Best Buy for $249.99 on November 2, but my card was charged twice for the same transaction. I authorized only one charge. Please reverse the duplicate $249.99 charge.”

b) By phone (if it’s easier)  
Call the number on the back of your credit card and say:
- “I need to dispute a **duplicate charge** on my credit card.”  
- Provide:
  - Merchant: **Best Buy**  
  - Amount: **$249.99**  
  - Posted date: **November 2**  
  - Explain: “I made one purchase, but there are **two identical charges**. I only authorized one.”

Ask them:
- For your **dispute/case number**  
- Whether they will issue a **temporary credit** while they investigate  
- If they need any documents uploaded/emailed (statement, receipt, etc.)

3) Should you contact Best Buy?
For a duplicate charge, it’s often helpful to do both:
- **Contact Best Buy customer service** (chat, phone, or in-store where you purchased) and say:
  > “I have two charges of $249.99 on my credit card for a single purchase I made on November 2. Can you reverse the duplicate charge on your end?”
- If they agree to refund:
  - Ask for a **reference/confirmation number** or a **written confirmation email**.  
  - Keep this as backup evidence for your card issuer.

4) What to watch for next
- Your bank may:
  - Post a **temporary credit** for the duplicate charge during investigation.  
  - Ask you to sign/submit a short **dispute form**—complete it promptly.
- Check your:
  - **Next 1–2 statements** to confirm the duplicate charge is reversed.  
  - **Online account** for any messages asking for more info.

If you tell me:
- Which bank/card (e.g., Chase, Citi, Capital One, Amex, etc.), and  
- Whether you’re using their app or website,  

I can give you very specific, click-by-click steps and a short note you can paste into their dispute form word-for-word.</action>

<action type="say">
Here’s how to do this in the **Chase mobile app** plus wording you can paste in.

Step‑by‑step in the Chase app (iOS or Android)

1. Open the **Chase** app and sign in.
2. On the home screen, tap your **credit card account** (the one with the Best Buy charge).
3. Scroll through **Transactions/Activity** to find the **Best Buy $249.99 charge on November 2**.
   - If you see **two identical Best Buy $249.99 charges** on or around Nov 2, you’ll repeat steps 4–8 for the one that’s the duplicate.
4. Tap on the specific **Best Buy $249.99** transaction you want to dispute.
5. On the transaction detail screen, look for and tap:
   - **“Dispute transaction”**, or
   - **“Something wrong with this transaction?”**, or a similar link/button near the bottom.
6. When prompted for the **reason**, choose the option closest to:
   - **“I was charged more than once for something”**, or
   - **“Duplicate charge”**, or **“I was billed twice for the same purchase.”**
7. In the **“Explain what happened” / notes / description** box, paste this:

   > I am disputing a duplicate charge. I made a single purchase at Best Buy for $249.99 on November 2, but my card was charged twice for the same transaction. I only authorized one charge of $249.99. Please reverse the duplicate $249.99 charge.  
   >  
   > Details:  
   > • Merchant: Best Buy  
   > • Amount: $249.99  
   > • Date posted: November 2  
   > • Issue: Two identical charges for one purchase

8. Follow the remaining prompts:
   - If Chase asks whether you **received the goods/services**, answer **yes** (since the issue is duplicate billing, not non‑receipt).
   - If they ask which charge is correct, indicate that **one** of the $249.99 charges is valid and the **other is a duplicate**.
9. Review your information and tap **Submit**.

After you submit

- You should see either a confirmation screen or a secure message in the app with a **case/dispute number**.  
- Save or screenshot that page for your records.  
- Over the next few days, watch for:
  - A **temporary credit** for the duplicate charge, and  
  - Any **secure message** from Chase asking for more info.

If you’d like, tell me exactly what options you see on the transaction screen (wording/buttons), and I can adjust these steps to match your screen precisely.</action>
